title: QuickBooks Online bank feed not updating
q: Why isn't my bank feed updating in QuickBooks Online?
why: The connection between QuickBooks and your bank broke. Common causes are a changed bank password, a new security or multi-factor step, the bank changing how it connects, or an account that was closed or renumbered.
fix: Go to Transactions (or Banking) and click the refresh or Update button for the account
If you see an error, sign in again with your current bank login and complete any security prompts
Check your bank's website for a notice about connection changes
If it still won't connect, download a .QBO or .CSV file from your bank and upload it for the missing dates
Avoid disconnecting and reconnecting with an earlier start date, which can pull in duplicates
pro: If transactions are missing for months, or you reconnected and now have duplicates, it's usually faster to have the account cleaned up and reconciled in one pass.

title: Reconciliation doesn't match your bank statement
q: Why doesn't my QuickBooks reconciliation match my bank statement?
why: A transaction from an already-reconciled period was edited, deleted or added after you reconciled, so the beginning balance no longer matches the statement. It can also come from a transaction entered twice or a deposit recorded for the wrong amount.
fix: Check that the beginning balance on the reconcile screen equals your statement's beginning balance
Open the reconciliation history for the account and view the report for the last good period to see changes made after reconciling
Look for duplicates, deleted transactions and amounts that are off by a transposed digit
Fix the changed transactions rather than forcing the difference with an adjustment
pro: If several months don't tie out, an accountant can undo and redo reconciliations from QuickBooks Online Accountant.

title: Uncategorized income, expenses and 'Ask My Accountant'
q: What do I do with uncategorized transactions in QuickBooks Online?
why: Transactions were added from the bank feed without a real category, so they land in Uncategorized Income, Uncategorized Expense or Ask My Accountant. Until they're recategorized, your Profit and Loss report, and any tax return based on it, will be wrong.
fix: Run a Profit and Loss report and click the uncategorized lines to see the transactions
Recategorize each one to the correct account
Set up bank rules for repeating vendors so the same transaction is categorized automatically next time
Do this monthly rather than at year end
pro: If there are hundreds of them, bulk cleanup with the Reclassify tool in QuickBooks Online Accountant is much faster than one at a time.

title: Payments to deposit (Undeposited Funds) balance is too high
q: Why is my Undeposited Funds balance so high in QuickBooks Online?
why: Customer payments were recorded against invoices but never grouped into a bank deposit. Then the real deposit from the bank feed was added as new income, so income is counted twice and the Payments to deposit account keeps growing.
fix: Open the Payments to deposit (Undeposited Funds) register to see the old payments
For each deposit on your bank statement, create a Bank Deposit (+ New, then Bank deposit) that groups the matching customer payments
In the bank feed, match the deposit to that Bank Deposit instead of adding it as income
For deposits already added as income, undo them in the bank feed's Categorized tab, then match them to the Bank Deposit
pro: A large old balance usually means income is overstated, which means you may be overpaying tax. It's worth fixing before you file.

title: Duplicate transactions from the bank feed
q: How do I fix duplicate transactions in QuickBooks Online?
why: The same transaction was entered by hand (an expense, bill payment or invoice payment) and then added again from the bank feed instead of being matched. Reconnecting a bank account can also download transactions a second time.
fix: In the bank feed, use Match when QuickBooks suggests an existing transaction instead of Add
Exclude feed items that are already in your books
Delete or void true duplicates only after checking they aren't in a reconciled period
Reconcile the account afterward to confirm the balance is right
pro: If duplicates are spread across reconciled months, cleanup needs care so reconciliations don't break.

title: Opening Balance Equity has a balance
q: What is Opening Balance Equity in QuickBooks Online and should it be zero?
why: QuickBooks posts to Opening Balance Equity when you enter starting balances for bank accounts, loans or other accounts. It's meant to be temporary and should normally be zero once your books are set up.
fix: Check which transactions make up the balance (run the account's QuickReport)
Confirm the opening balances were correct as of your start date
Have the balance moved to owner's equity or retained earnings, as appropriate for your business type
pro: How it should be closed depends on whether you're a sole proprietor, partnership or S corporation, so this one is best handled by your tax preparer. We can do it for you.

title: Loan payments recorded as an expense
q: How do I record a loan payment in QuickBooks Online?
why: Only the interest part of a loan payment is an expense. The principal part reduces the loan balance. If the whole payment is categorized as an expense, your profit is understated and the loan balance on your balance sheet is wrong.
fix: Set up the loan as a liability account
Split each payment: principal to the loan account, interest to an interest expense account
Use your lender's statement or amortization schedule for the split
Reconcile the loan account to the lender's statement at least yearly
pro: If the loan paid for a vehicle or equipment, that asset also needs to be set up for depreciation, so it's worth getting these right before tax time.

title: Personal expenses paid from the business account
q: How do I record personal expenses paid from my business account in QuickBooks?
why: Personal spending isn't a business expense. Recording it as one overstates your deductions, which is a common issue the IRS looks for.
fix: Create an equity account for owner draws (sole proprietor or LLC) or shareholder distributions (S corporation)
Categorize personal purchases to that equity account, not to an expense
Set up a bank rule if the same personal charges repeat
Better still, use a personal card or account for personal spending
pro: For S corporations, distributions and owner salary have tax consequences (owners who work in the business must take a reasonable salary), so it's worth reviewing them with us before year end.

title: Preparing 1099s in QuickBooks Online
q: How do I prepare 1099-NEC forms in QuickBooks Online?
why: If you paid an unincorporated contractor $2,000 or more for services in 2026 ($600 for 2025 and earlier), you generally need to issue a Form 1099-NEC. QuickBooks can prepare them, but only if vendors and accounts are set up correctly.
fix: Collect a Form W-9 from each contractor before paying them
Mark those vendors as 1099 eligible and enter their tax ID
Map your contractor expense accounts in the 1099 setup
Review the 1099 report, then file and send forms by January 31
Payments made by credit card or through apps like PayPal are generally excluded, since those processors report them
pro: Missing W-9s and wrong tax IDs are the usual problem. Late or incorrect 1099s can bring IRS penalties.

title: Months behind on bookkeeping
q: How do I catch up on months of bookkeeping in QuickBooks Online?
why: It happens to most small business owners: the bank feed piles up, receipts get lost, and tax time arrives with books that aren't ready.
fix: Download statements for every bank and credit card account for the missing months
Make sure each account's starting balance matches the first statement
Work through the bank feed month by month, using bank rules for repeat transactions
Reconcile each month as you finish it
Review the profit and loss for anything that looks off before filing taxes
